mechanism: "addresstype" and "changetype" are DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS rows (src/config-options.lisp:435, :438) and grep finds no reader. There is no per-wallet default to hold them either: no WALLET-DEFAULT-ADDRESS-TYPE or WALLET-DEFAULT-CHANGE-TYPE symbol exists in BITCOIN-LISP.WALLET. Both RPCs hardcode the fallback -- (%address-type-arg (second params) :bech32) in getnewaddress (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1822) and (%address-type-arg (first params) :bech32) in getrawchangeaddress (:1846) -- while the per-call address_type argument is fully implemented, so the mechanism exists and only its configured default is missing. The automatic change type is the same story: %TRANSACTION-CHANGE-TYPE (src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:1534-1557) takes (wallet change-type recipients) and is called with (wcc-change-type cc) at :1959-1960, and WCC-CHANGE-TYPE is only ever set from the per-call change_type option (:2777-2786) -- never from configuration. Core at d3056bc parses GetArg("-addresstype","") into m_default_address_type and GetArg("-changetype","") into m_default_change_type in CWallet::LoadWalletArgs, refusing to load the wallet on an unknown value (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:2956-2972); getnewaddress uses m_default_address_type (wallet/rpc/addresses.cpp:53), getrawchangeaddress uses m_default_change_type.value_or(m_default_address_type) (:99), and CreateTransaction passes m_default_change_type into TransactionChangeType (wallet/spend.cpp:1092). Worth recording because it bounds the consequence: our %TRANSACTION-CHANGE-TYPE otherwise matches CWallet::TransactionChangeType (wallet.cpp:2253-2312) branch for branch, including the final has_bech32m / has_bech32 fallbacks; the only unreachable branch is Core's "if m_default_address_type is legacy, use legacy", which cannot fire for us because our default is fixed at bech32.
consequence: An operator who set addresstype=bech32m to receive on taproot keeps being handed P2WPKH addresses from a bare getnewaddress, and changetype is ignored, so an operator who forced a change type to defeat the change-detection heuristic does not get it. No funds are at risk and no key material is affected -- the wallet can still issue every type on request, and the automatic change-type heuristic still matches the payment type, which is the privacy-preserving direction. Bounded on both sides that matter: the options are always explicitly supplied, so the startup WARN names them (measured), and the divergence is visible in the very first output the operator looks at -- the address prefix is tb1q/bc1q rather than tb1p/bc1p. Also unlike Core we accept an unknown value silently where Core refuses to load the wallet, but that is subsumed by the same warning. S3.
evidence: Executed in the project container (worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-options-s3, warm image, probes ga11probe/p-rest.lisp function P-ADDRTYPE and ga11probe/p-addr2.lisp function P-ADDR2). (a) End to end on a real testnet4 wallet (fresh temp datadir, rpc-createwallet "aptest", 4 external and 4 internal SPKMs including bech32m): a bare (rpc-getnewaddress node '()) returned "tb1qm2jqrcfkzqwqr97d3d55gh3exywpf8wq8yv6sq" (P2WPKH) and a bare (rpc-getrawchangeaddress node '()) returned "tb1qseux465ptr6nczhzxasumpeclupsw2lwpu7pws", while the explicit forms returned bech32m -- "tb1pde44ukkld5mlj4t8ggnf6e3v9a45e6vmgluyw93n575df9q6eyxqgpdzhq" and "tb1pag6dk598zf8xu5gskhved6plegn4he36pc6lxhlx04vj4nxd3pjq3srpkv" -- confirming the per-call mechanism works and only the configured default is absent. (b) The same image had already shown that -addresstype=bech32m -changetype=bech32m reach no start-node keyword: START-NODE-PLIST returned (:LISTEN T :WALLET-NAMES NIL :NETWORK :REGTEST) with both names in SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS. (c) (bl.wallet::%address-type-arg nil :bech32) => :BECH32; (find-symbol "WALLET-DEFAULT-ADDRESS-TYPE" "BITCOIN-LISP.WALLET") => NIL and likewise for WALLET-DEFAULT-CHANGE-TYPE; (function-lambda-list #'%transaction-change-type) => (WALLET CHANGE-TYPE RECIPIENTS), no configuration input. Sources: src/config-options.lisp:435,438; src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1805-1849; src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:264, 1534-1557, 1959-1960, 2777-2786; refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/init.cpp:46,48; refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:2253-2312, 2956-2972; refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/rpc/addresses.cpp:53,99; refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/spend.cpp:1092.
fix_shape: Give the wallet the two defaults Core gives it and read them from real options. Add DEFAULT-ADDRESS-TYPE (defaulting to :bech32, Core's DEFAULT_ADDRESS_TYPE) and DEFAULT-CHANGE-TYPE (defaulting to NIL, Core's empty std::optional) to the wallet -- or, to avoid a defstruct layout change and its fresh-FASL cold lane, to the wallet manager, which every one of these call sites can already reach -- and set them where the wallet is loaded, from new real DEFINE-OPTION "addresstype" and "changetype" rows parsed with %PARSE-OUTPUT-TYPE and rejected at startup on an unknown value with Core's exact wording ("Unknown address type '%s'" / "Unknown change type '%s'"). Then replace the three hardcoded fallbacks: getnewaddress's :bech32 becomes the default address type, getrawchangeaddress's becomes (or default-change-type default-address-type) exactly as wallet/rpc/addresses.cpp:99 does, and %CREATE-TRANSACTION-INTERNAL passes (or (wcc-change-type cc) default-change-type) into %TRANSACTION-CHANGE-TYPE, matching wallet/spend.cpp:1092. Port Core's "if the default address type is legacy, use legacy for change" branch at the top of %TRANSACTION-CHANGE-TYPE at the same time, since it becomes reachable the moment -addresstype can be legacy. A test should start a wallet with each configured type and assert the bare getnewaddress / getrawchangeaddress prefix follows it, with the unset case asserted to stay bech32 as the positive control.
